plant.metric: scan free-run P50 |x err| 352 nm @128, ~6x better than the TCN in the slow-scan regime the controller operates in; one-step 0.9 nm. NB worse on fast ID excitation (P95 6.4% @128, fails the 5% gate the TCN passes) - promoted on the scan metric of record
plant.note: windowed larger delta SSM (d_model 128, d_state 64, 4 layers, val 2.7e-5). Best plant for the controller's slow-scan operating regime. Recurrent streaming refuted - see reports/decoupled_plant_hypothesis.md. UNITS: the 352 nm scan metric was computed on a units-mismatched Brett replay (raw counts fed into the nm-scale plant); units-corrected, both plants diverge open-loop on real scans and the '6x better' does not hold - metric under review, see reports/_UNITS_CORRECTION.md. LONG-HORIZON (2026-08-26, SUPERSEDES the 'best plant for the operating regime' claim above): this SSM DIVERGES in closed loop past ~100 steps - its unbounded recurrent state runs away under autoregression (reanchor=0 hold blows up ~97k->1.3M nm by 8000 steps). SHORT-HORIZON-ONLY; never roll it beyond ~100 steps. For any long-horizon use (controller-training rollouts, endurance sim, seconds-to-hours scans) use the TCN (champion:plant_tcn), stationary at the ~20 nm floor. champion:plant still points here for back-compat - resolve champion:plant_tcn for long-horizon. See reports/long_horizon_control.md

plant_tcn.metric: ID-split P95 position drift within the 5% gate to step 128 (fast-excitation regime)
plant_tcn.note: M1 rollout champion; best on fast ID-like motion via the RF>window recency bias. Retained as the windowed-TCN architecture champion - complementary to the SSM, not superseded. LONG-HORIZON CHAMPION (2026-08-26): TCN + integral controller is STATIONARY in closed loop (reanchor=0: ~12 nm P50 / ~22 nm P95 on x, flat over 8000 steps, at the ~20 nm HW floor) because its bounded window cannot accumulate, unlike the SSM's recurrent state which runs away. This is the plant for all long-horizon work (controller training, endurance sim, seconds-to-hours) - resolve champion:plant_tcn for it. See reports/long_horizon_control.md
